title: Norway Fans Row Their Way to World Cup Fame!
summary:
Imagine riding an escalator and suddenly hearing a group of people shouting "Row! Row! Row!" while pretending to row a boat. That's exactly what happened at Boston's South Station during the World Cup. A reporter named Jeremy Siegel filmed it, and the video went viral. The fans were from Norway, and they were doing what's now called the "Viking Row." They wore Viking helmets and pulled imaginary oars together.

Norway hasn't been in the World Cup for 28 years, so fans were super excited. They beat Iraq 4-1 in their first game. The Viking Row became their rallying cry. Even the speaker of Norway's parliament, Masud Gharahkhani, led a rowing session in parliament! He said they do it for peace, love, and to support their team.

Norway is a small country with only 5.6 million people, but their fans are making a big noise. One mom, Veslemoy Aga, said watching Norway in the World Cup with her three soccer-crazy sons has been magical. The whole country is dreaming of winning the cup.
why_it_matters: Even a small country's joy can spread around the world, showing how team spirit and a fun chant can bring people together, just like cheering for your school team.
